acceptance: Read docs/04/supervisor_dispatch_refactor_proposal_2026-08-04.md section 'Problem 6' in full before starting -- it contains the confirmed live repro (PR #4532 head 4aae7942 was review_approved at 13:39:50, then commit b84acd1e3003 six minutes later -- a 2-line task-brief closeout note -- invalidated that exact approval and forced a second full review round-trip for zero code change).

Find and remove whatever workflow/finalize step commits a post-approval 'closeout record' write to .orchestrator/task-briefs/*.md after review_approved. The live task-state written by ai_status.py's approve command already durably records the approval; a redundant git-committed copy created AFTER the reviewed diff is not needed and is actively harmful because it moves the exact head the approval is bound to.

If a durable git-reachable evidence record of approval is still wanted for recovery paths like reconcile_merged_done, it must be produced as part of the SAME commit/diff the reviewer reviews and approves once -- never as a follow-up commit after approval. Do not simply relocate the same after-the-fact write to a different file; fix the ordering.

As defense in depth (not a substitute for the above): teach scripts/git/github_review_bridge.py's exact-head binding check to treat a commit landing after review_approved that touches ONLY paths under .orchestrator/task-briefs/ as a no-op relative to the reviewed content, and carry the existing approval forward onto the new head automatically instead of forcing a second review pass. This should rarely fire once the root habit above is removed -- it exists only to catch cases you can't fully control (e.g. legacy worker behavior).

Add a regression test: review_approved -> task-brief-only commit -> approval must still hold (either because no such commit gets produced anymore, or because the carry-forward exemption catches it) -- assert the task does NOT bounce back into a fresh review cycle for a diff containing zero code changes.
Do not touch poll_workers, process_queue, dispatch_ready_tasks, or reconcile_queue_records.

task_spec.summary: A live incident on 2026-08-04: this fleet's own finalize step writes a 'closeout record' commit to a task's task-brief file immediately after review_approved, purely to document that approval happened -- and that commit's changed head invalidates the exact-head-bound approval it exists to record, forcing a pointless second review round-trip. Standard code review never produces a commit as a side effect of approving one; this habit is redundant with the live task-state ai_status.py approve already durably records, and self-defeating. Remove the habit at the source; add a narrow carry-forward exemption as a safety net only.
task_spec.title: Stop writing a post-approval closeout commit that invalidates its own review
